jobs.name: OPS L0 Heartbeat Meta-Loop (SLA breach watcher)

payload.message:
OPS L0 META-LOOP — run now.

You are the L0 meta-loop. L0 is a lightweight bash heartbeat (workspace/scripts/l0-heartbeat.sh) that scans workspace/ops/alerts/<UTCSTAMP>_L0.txt and the system for OPEN tickets whose SLA deadline has passed and writes alerts to workspace/ops/alerts/<UTCSTAMP>_L0.txt.

ABOUT THE L0 ALERT FILE FORMAT (read carefully — this is the source of past bugs):
  L0 writes files with this structure:
    L0-heartbeat @ <UTC>
    workspace: /Users/redinside/.openclaw/workspace
    alerts: N
    ---
    SLA-BREACH: <ticket-id> | <priority> | <deadline> | breached by <amt>
    CRITICAL: <system-level error message, e.g. "cron jobs count = ERR (expected >0)">
  L0 has TWO distinct line prefixes after the '---' separator:
    - "SLA-BREACH:" for per-ticket SLA breaches (needs ticket-id lookup)
    - "CRITICAL:" for system-level health failures (no ticket-id; just an error string)
  A consumer that only matches "SLA-BREACH:" will silently swallow every "CRITICAL:" line
  (e.g. the recurring "CRITICAL: cron jobs count = ERR"). The fix is to accept BOTH prefixes
  AND to page on the file's "alerts: N" header count being > 0, even if no SLA-BREACH line is present.
  Do not re-introduce a single-prefix matcher. If a third prefix is ever added to L0, this spec
  should be updated to include it.

STEPS:
1. Run L0: bash /Users/redinside/.openclaw/workspace/scripts/l0-heartbeat.sh 2>&1 | tail -20
2. Inspect the NEWEST alert file: ls -t /Users/redinside/.openclaw/workspace/ops/alerts/*_L0.txt 2>/dev/null | head -1
3. If the file has size 0 bytes OR does not exist: return NO_REPLY (everything is green).
4. Read the file's "alerts: N" header. If N == 0 (or the file is empty / missing): return NO_REPLY.
5. If N > 0, extract every non-blank line after the '---' separator. Each line will be one of:
     SLA-BREACH: <ticket-id> | <priority> | <deadline> | breached by <amt>
     CRITICAL:   <system-level error message>
   Treat BOTH prefixes as page-worthy. (Previously this spec only matched SLA-BREACH: lines,
   which caused CRITICAL: lines to be silently dropped — that bug class must not return.)
6. For each extracted line:
   a. If the line starts with "SLA-BREACH:": confirm the ticket still has Status: OPEN in
      workspace/ops/TICKET-TRACKER.md (L0 only flags OPEN tickets). Cross-check
      workspace/ops/LEARNINGS.md for prior handling of this exact ticket-id.
   b. If the line starts with "CRITICAL:": no ticket lookup needed; this is a system-level
      health failure. The text after "CRITICAL: " is the error description. Cross-check
      workspace/ops/LEARNINGS.md '## L0 Detections' for prior handling of this exact
      "CRITICAL: <text>" fingerprint in the last 6h (see RULES below).
7. If at least one line is page-worthy (either prefix, passing the 6h de-dup check), send
   ONE consolidated Telegram DM to user id 1012034994 in this format:
     🚨 L0 alert: <count> issue(s) in workspace/ops/alerts/<file>:
       🚨 [1/N] SLA-BREACH: <ticket-id> (<priority>) — breached by <amt>
       🚨 [2/N] CRITICAL: <error text>
       ...
   Include BOTH prefix types in the numbered list, in the order they appear in the file.
   If N == 1, drop the [1/N] numbering.
8. Append ONE bullet per page-worthy line to workspace/ops/LEARNINGS.md under '## L0 Detections'
   (create the section if missing). For SLA-BREACH lines:
     - <UTCSTAMP> L0 fired on <ticket-id> (<priority>, breached by <amt>). Action: Telegram DM sent.
   For CRITICAL lines:
     - <UTCSTAMP> L0 fired on CRITICAL: <error text>. Action: Telegram DM sent.
9. If the alerts: N > 0 but every line was suppressed by the 6h de-dup rule: still append
   ONE summary bullet:
     - <UTCSTAMP> L0 fired, <N> alert(s) in <file>; all suppressed by 6h de-dup window.

RULES:
